daily.title: New York Archdiocese to pay $800 million to sex abuse survivors
daily.summary: Around 1,300 survivors agreed to the $800 million payout from the Catholic Church, marking one of the largest clergy abuse settlements in the US.

daily.title: Nigeria: Tinubu launches reelection bid amid economic woes
daily.summary: President Bola Tinubu promised "a better tomorrow" for Nigerians while kicking off his next electoral campaign, while also blaming his rivals for poverty plaguing Africa's most populous nation.

daily.title: Ukraine: Starlink satellite speeds restored to normal
daily.summary: The announcement comes after Starlink and Starshield restrictions had disrupted military operations in Ukraine and sparked tensions with the US.

daily.title: German national facing trial for alleged attempt to join IS
daily.summary: A 21-year-old suspect is being held in pre-trial detention for allegedly trying to join the "Islamic State" terror group.

daily.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
daily.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

daily.title: Will Guinea-Bissau remain trapped in political chaos?
daily.summary: Elections scheduled for December 6 in Guinea-Bissau have been postponed indefinitely. No new date has been set, leaving the country's return to civilian rule uncertain.

daily.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
daily.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

daily.title: Germany news: Merz calls for unity at CSU party conference
daily.summary: With his coalition under pressure, Merz delivered an address at the close of the CSU conference in Munich. Meanwhile, fire has largely destroyed Hitler's former Eagle's Nest retreat. DW has more

daily.title: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travels to Chinese border city via newly opened bridge
daily.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travelled to China’s border city of Dandong via a newly opened bridge linking the two countries, where he met a senior Chinese official.

daily.title: France: Clashes break out as protests go nationwide
daily.summary: Police and elite security forces were out in force in French cities as tens of thousands participated in protests on Saturday. The situation turned tense toward the end of protests in several cities, including Paris.

daily.title: Why Russia's arrest of Japanese journalist is the latest sign of deteriorating ties between the countries.
daily.summary: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.

daily.title: Taiwan: Typhoon Champi leaves 1 dead, over 500 injured
daily.summary: After killing one person and causing major disruptions in Taiwan, Typhoon Champi is now headed towards China.

daily.title: India news: Neha Bora refuses to sign peace bond, cites right to democratic dissent
daily.summary: Neha Bora says the peace bond violates the right to democratic dissent. The statement comes amid a wider protest calling for the removal of India's election chief. DW has more.

weekly.title: Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat catches fire, police say
weekly.summary: Authorities have arrested a suspect as firemen try to put out the fire in Bavaria, near the Austrian border.

weekly.title: France to deploy 70,000 police officers ahead of protests
weekly.summary: With new protests in France planned for this weekend, the authorities pledged to do everything in their power to prevent looting, violence and vandalism.

weekly.title: Ebola: Kenya announces second death
weekly.summary: Kenyan health officials said the 65-year-old ​woman was a close ‌relative of a ‌​man who died of Ebola last month. The woman developed symptoms ‌while under quarantine in Nairobi.

weekly.title: Trump eases Canada tariffs ahead of US midterms
weekly.summary: The move comes as Trump's Republican Party scrambles to maintain control of the US Congress, with a Republican candidate in a key Senate race saying she had lobbied to lift the tariffs on Canadian products.

weekly.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
weekly.summary: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

weekly.title: Jordan: Karak church shooting leaves 7 dead, dozens injured
weekly.summary: A shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Jordan happened during a funeral, according to authorities. Two unidentified men opened fire on the procession, with Jordan's king vowing "the harshest retaliation."

weekly.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
weekly.summary: The Ukrainian city of Oleshky, occupied by Russia and on the frontline, faces a humanitarian crisis. The localized truce comes as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said negotiators would meet for wider talks next month.

weekly.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
weekly.summary: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

weekly.title: Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
weekly.summary: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

weekly.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
weekly.summary: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

weekly.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
weekly.summary: Names are central to our identity, so what happens when that name is a source of ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

weekly.title: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
weekly.summary: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

weekly.title: Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
weekly.summary: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
weekly.summary: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

weekly.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the AfD gains ground?
weekly.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

weekly.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker?
weekly.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is the clear front-runner for football's most prestigious individual prize, which will be awarded on Monday. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

weekly.title: Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
weekly.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

weekly.title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
weekly.summary: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.

weekly.title: Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
weekly.summary: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

weekly.title: Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
weekly.summary: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

weekly.title: Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
weekly.summary: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

weekly.title: Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
weekly.summary: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.

weekly.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
weekly.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

weekly.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
weekly.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

weekly.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
weekly.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

weekly.title: New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
weekly.summary: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security.

weekly.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

weekly.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
weekly.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

weekly.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
weekly.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

weekly.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
weekly.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

weekly.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
weekly.summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

weekly.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
weekly.summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

weekly.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
weekly.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

weekly.title: What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
weekly.summary: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.

weekly.title: France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
weekly.summary: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

weekly.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
weekly.summary: Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

weekly.title: How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
weekly.summary: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

weekly.title: Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
weekly.summary: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

developing.title: Live: Fresh protests hit France amid heightened security
developing.summary: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as thousands participate in a new round of protests. The protest location was changed last minute in Paris. Follow DW.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
